ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory identification and ongoing due diligence on all shareholders, directors, and UBOs under Ley 10/2010. Screening must include the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions committees, OFAC SDN list, and Spanish SEPBLAC indicators. Enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, and source-of-wealth verification are required for PEPs and their close associates; any UBO hit on a sanctions list prevents the incorporation file from proceeding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Sede Electrónica del Registro Mercantil Central - Expediente de certificación negativa de denominación social
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be expressed in Spanish or in an accepted foreign-language derivation transliterated into the Spanish alphabet; the name must be distinguishable from existing denominations and must not be misleading as to the corporate object. The statutory suffix 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or the abbreviation 'S.L.' is added after registration and may not be used as the core distinctive element of the approved name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A negative-name certificate is valid for 90 days and is not statutorily extendable; if incorporation does not occur within that period, a new name application must be submitted. Upon rejection because of identity or confusing similarity with an existing denomination, the applicant may file an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within one month of notification. The appeal must set out the proposed name, the refusal grounds, and evidence of District distinctiveness. If the name was rejected because it contains a prohibited or reserved token, the applicant must first obtain ministerial authorization from the competent authority and then resubmit. If the administrative appeal is dismissed, a contentious-administrative appeal may be brought before the Audiencia Nacional within two months of notification.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible as the initial registered-address solution provided it corresponds to a real Spanish address, is staffed or serviced to receive official notifications during business hours, and is not merely a PO box. For a cybersecurity SaaS business, virtual-office-only substance carries enhanced tax-residence risk because the corporate income-tax residence test looks to the registered office and place of effective management; a virtual maildrop without local management may be challenged by the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate. Estimated 20-25% probability of an unannounced inspection within the first 24 months by the tax administration, SEPBLAC, or the commercial registry, with materially higher probability if only a virtual office is maintained and no local commercial substance is demonstrable.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Articles 21-30, 62, 210 and 214)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central and the relevant Provincial Mercantile Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation) presented for registration in the Mercantile Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid in cash at incorporation; the capital must be deposited in a Spanish bank account, evidenced by a bank certificate, and left unwithdrawn until registration (Article 62 LSC)
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The shareholders unanimously resolve to: (i) adopt the draft articles of association submitted to this meeting, thereby forming the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada; (ii) subscribe and fully pay the entire share capital of EUR 3,000, divided equally into 1,000 participations, and acknowledge the corresponding bank deposit certificate; (iii) adopt a registered office located at the address stated in the deed; (iv) appoint the designated director and chief executive officer, granting them the widest powers of representation and management available under law; and (v) commence all necessary filings with the Mercantile Registry and tax authorities. Each resolution is individually approved by unanimous shareholder consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit electronically or in person an official application for a negative name certificate (certificación negativa de denominación social). The application must include three preferred unique names in order of priority, the proposed corporate purpose, and the identity details of the founding shareholder(s). The certificate is valid for three months and proves no registered company currently holds the chosen name.
required_dossiers: Completed application form for denominación social
Copy of the founding shareholder's passport/ID
Draft articles of association
Proof of payment of the name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name conflict is detected, file a further application with alternative names. If the certificate is wrongly denied, submit an appeal (recurso) to the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Spanish Corporate Bank Account and Deposit Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate account in the name of the company in formation. Deposit the minimum share capital (EUR 3,000) or the full subscribed capital if greater. Request a bank certificate specifying the account holder, account number, currency, amount deposited, and the shareholder(s) making the deposit. This certificate must be presented to the notary when executing the deed.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate
Draft deed and articles of association
Passport / NIE of all subscribing shareholders
Anti-money laundering compliance forms and source of funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional KYC documentation, promptly provide personal tax identification numbers, proof of address, and a short business plan. Should the bank refuse the account for institutional reasons, select another Spanish bank; no regulatory authorization is needed for a standard SL deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Public Deed of Incorporation Before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before a notary in the province of the registered office. The notary will review the bank deposit certificate, statutory clauses, and shareholder identification. All shareholders must sign the public deed (escritura de constitución). The notary will then submit the deed to the Mercantile Registry and issue a copy for tax filing purposes. The deed must include the statutes, capital structure, board composition if any, and registered office.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate
Bank deposit certificate
Draft articles of association
Passport / NIE of each shareholder and director
Statutory declaration of non-conviction for directors
Spanish CIF/NIF provisional form (modelo 036) cross-reference if available
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects in the draft deed or missing signatures, correct the documents and reschedule the notarial appointment. A new bank certificate is not required if the deposit remains unchanged; otherwise, refresh the certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pay Transfer Tax and Stamp Duty (ITP-AJD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Tributaria de la Comunidad Autónoma (Regional Tax Office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 business days of the deed's execution, file the corporation form (modelo 600) with the regional tax authority and pay the Stamp Duty (Actos Jurídicos Documentados) on the share capital increase and notarial document. The typical rate ranges from 0.5% to 1.5% depending on the autonomous community. The payment certificate must accompany the application for registration at the Mercantile Registry.
required_dossiers: First copy of the public deed
Modelo 600 tax form (duly completed and stamped)
Proof of payment of ITP-AJD
Bank certificate of deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the regional tax office applies an incorrect higher rate, submit a rectification request (escrito de rectificación) within the applicable limitation period. Late filing penalties may be waived via diligent voluntary submission (régimen de regularización voluntaria) if no formal inspection has started.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company and Obtain Final Tax Identification Number (CIF/NIF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry and Agencia Tributaria (Spanish Tax Agency)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the public deed plus the model 036 form and the AJD payment receipt at the Mercantile Registry. The registry will issue a registration order and the company is considered fully incorporated. Following registration, the tax agency will issue the definitive CIF (Código de Identificación Fiscal). Provisional NIF (CIF provisional) can also be applied for pre-registration to facilitate contracting. Finally, register the company for corporation tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades), VAT (IVA) and, if applicable, as an employer.
required_dossiers: Original public deed and a certified copy
AJD payment certificate
Modelo 036 registration form
Application for the Mercantile Registry registration
Directors' identification and tax reference copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Mercantile Registry issues a defect note (nota de calificación), correct the indicated defects (usually missing documents or clause inconsistencies) and re-submit. If registration is refused due to substantive legal issues, file an administrative appeal before the Registry Directorate (Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública) within two months.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ayuntamiento de la localidad where the registered office is located (Municipal Town Hall – Concejalía de Actividades / Urbanismo)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Actividad y Apertura (Municipal Activity and Opening License for office / commercial use)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO) for state-level assessment, and the competent regional environmental authority for municipal environmental review
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Category Minor: Office-based cyber security SaaS activity is not subject to a full EIA; it requires a simplified municipal environmental compatibility assessment (memoria ambiental) covering noise, waste, and energy consumption.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge permitted; office sewage connection to municipal sewerage only. Compliance with municipal noise limits (typically ≤ 35 dB(A) at night indoors). Electronic waste, toner cartridges and hazardous battery waste must be managed under Royal Decree 110/2015 (WEEE) and Ley 7/2022 on waste and contaminated soils, with zero tolerance for direct landfilling of data-bearing media.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (certificado de protección contra incendios) from the authorized municipal technical service or a qualified inspector, ensuring compliance with CTE DB-SI (Safety in Case of Fire). Structural load inspection of server rooms and meeting rooms from a competent architect/engineer (ITE/ensayo estructural) if floor loading exceeds residential norms. Occupational health and safety clearance under Ley 31/1995, including an initial risk assessment and a workplace safety plan, approved by an accredited prevention service.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Sede Electrónica
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains its definitive NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) automatically upon incorporation through the notarized public deed filed with the Mercantile Registry; foreign entities without a permanent establishment must apply for a non-resident NIF via AEAT Form 030 or 036/037, appointing a tax representative when required, before engaging in Spanish-source taxable activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election under Spanish law; an SL is considered a per-se corporate taxpayer fully subject to the Impuesto sobre Sociedades. Available elective regimes include the consolidated tax group regime (Régimen de Consolidación Fiscal), the special ETVE regime, patent box, and tax transparency for certain jointly-held assets; hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD (Law 11/2021) apply non-electively.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido) – Spanish VAT
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None for established businesses (compulsory registration from the first taxable supply in Spain). For intra-EU distance sales and cross-border B2C telecommunications/e-services, the €10,000 annual pan-EU threshold applies with mandatory OSS registration for e-commerce supplies to final consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) requires real-time transmission of VAT transaction records via AEAT web services/API for taxpayers with turnover above €6 million, members of VAT groups, or those in certain regimes; general B2B e-invoicing is phased in under Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece), using interoperable formats; compliant billing software and solutions accredited under Verifactu (Reglamento 1007/2023) with certified electronic signatures; no general pre-clearance digital stamping for small and medium entities.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods are exempt with right to deduction (0% VAT) under Article 21 LIVA provided the goods leave the EU customs territory within three months and the exporter retains prescribed evidence. For cybersecurity SaaS (electronically supplied services), B2B supplies to non-established business customers fall outside Spanish VAT (reverse charge for EU; outside scope for non-EU), and B2C supplies to non-EU final customers are generally outside Spanish VAT when the service is effectively used outside Spain; no formal zero-rating claim is required for services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUE/DUA) and customs clearance certificate
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill
Proof of physical departure (carrier documents, terminal receipts, container tracking)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer/FX documentation evidencing payment receipt
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unjustified zero-rated claims trigger retroactive VAT assessment with late-payment interest, a 10% to 150% surcharge depending on base, or a 50% minimum penalty under Spanish tax law; knowingly false documentation can constitute criminal tax fraud if defrauded amount exceeds €120,000, with penalties of imprisonment and/or fines. The AEAT imposes retrospective clawbacks and monetary sanctions on exporters that fail to satisfy the documentary and substantive conditions within the statutory period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) as the central banking authority on balance-of-payments statistics and monetary supervision, in coordination with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones of the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism for foreign investment and export/import regulation and the Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV) for FX derivatives conduct regulation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible in Spain. Current account and capital account transactions are liberalized under Article 63 TFEU and the Spanish Foreign Investment Law. No exchange-control licensing applies to software-as-a-service exports, dividend repatriations, loan amortizations or equity liquidation proceeds. Administrative filing duties remain, primarily the statistical disclosure of cross-border payments and the post-filing registration of foreign direct investment; no currency conversion or central bank approval is required for making or receiving payments in EUR.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no statutory surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. SaaS/cybersecurity export receipts freely remain in EUR or authorized FX accounts. However, payments and receipts from non-residents exceeding the current reporting threshold must be reported to Banco de España via the electronic foreign-transaction declaration framework; the threshold for transactions requiring declaration is EUR 50,000 or equivalent unless the transaction is already reported under investment-registry rules. The obligation is statistical and AML-driven, not exchange-control approval.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for statutory capital escrow and dividend repatriation; Medium for operational collections and vendor payments. Spanish-recognized Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) passported from the EEA, such as established EU fintech platforms, may be used as supplementary banking rails. Offshore EMIs without EEA license or Spanish registration are unusable for foreign investment registry compliance, statutory capital certification, operator accounts and official bank officer certificate requirements. For an ES_SL treasury structure, an EU/EEA-licensed EMI is acceptable only after the principal domestic bank account is open and the foreign investment declaration is secured.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish anti-money-laundering rules do not categorically mandate a physical in-branch appearance of directors or UBOs. Remote onboarding is commonly permitted using videoconference identity verification complemented by notarized identification, apostilled corporate documents and sworn translations into Spanish. In practice, major Spanish banks often request an in-person interview or a Spanish notary-attested remote session when the shareholder structure is non-resident, multi-country or high-wealth; banking policy, not statute, drives the mandate. The safest execution path is a brief physical visit to Spain by the ultimate signatory or a formal notarial power of attorney granted to an in-country representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate shareholder or opaque ownership chain that prevents clear UBO identification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled company registry certificate (certificación registral) for the corporate shareholder and the Spanish SL, sworn Spanish translation, notarized UBO declaration (declaración de titular real) signed by all shareholders, corporate ownership chart showing the natural-person ultimate beneficial owners, share register, tax residence certificate of the corporate shareholder, and board resolutions authorizing the account opening and signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection sourced from cryptocurrency, payment-platform float or third-party settlement flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three months of bank statements from the originator bank, SWIFT confirmation of the correspondent routing, cryptocurrency-to-fiat exit trail if crypto was used, merchant settlement reports from SaaS payment processors, signed commercial agreements for the relevant cybersecurity subscription contracts, audited or internally certified financial statements, and a written source-of-capital statement by a Spanish registered auditor (ICAC).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cybersecurity activity flagged as dual-use, network-surveillance, government-intrusion or anonymity-enabling.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Technical whitepaper demonstrating cloud vulnerability scanning and authorized penetration testing scope; EU Dual-Use Regulation export classification self-assessment; client acceptance policy limiting services to contractual customers; prohibition of malware/intrusion tooling in standard terms; ISO/IEC 27001 certificate; cybersecurity insurance policy; and a transaction-specific legal opinion from a Spanish law firm confirming that the services are not within restrictive EU sanctions regimes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP status, politically exposed persons, or residence in a high-risk third country.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent PEP due-diligence questionnaire, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declaration with documented proof, notarized passport or national ID, proof of lawful residence and occupation, professional and bank references, court records or criminal-checks certificate from the country of residence, and clearance letter from a compliance consultant or EU counsel.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident shareholder wires EUR to the Spanish SL's operational or escrow account using SWIFT MT103 with a clearly stated payment reference 'Contribución al capital social' or 'Aportación dineraria a fondo perdido' for share capital. The receiving IBAN is Spanish (ES format) under the exact corporate name of the ES_SL. Verification requires: certificate of performance of the capital increase at the Spanish Commercial Registry, notarial deed if the capital injection accompanies corporate documentation, and foreign investment registration disclosure to the Banco de España. For inbound shareholder loans, the payment reference must identify 'Préstamo accionista' and the interest tax consequences are assessed separately under Spanish thin-capitalization and withholding rules.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational funds are cleared through SWIFT MT103 for international SaaS subscription fees, subcontractors, infrastructure providers and software licences; EUR payments within the EEA may use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant. Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700) are generally inapplicable to pure-play cybersecurity SaaS and should be reserved for hardware purchasing or buyer-required documentary protection. Each outbound wire must include the beneficiary legal identity, tax ID (NIF/EU VAT), invoice reference and the statistical purpose code from the Bank of Spain balance-of-payments classification. Dividends to foreign shareholders are settled via MT103 after corporate approval and are subject to Spanish withholding tax and treaty relief if applicable.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX contracts for immediate conversion of USD, GBP or other receipts into EUR
Plain-vanilla OTC FX forwards with an EU credit institution, with documented underlying commercial exposure
FX swaps (swap de divisas) to manage temporary mismatches between receipt and payment dates
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for material multi-year USD-denominated infrastructure contracts
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in non-convertible EMEA currencies where no onshore deliverable market exists, subject to CNMV-eligible counterparty and demonstrable translation/transaction exposure
